title: Round 8 / ECDLP-24: sourced classification of weak ECDLP curve families
question: Which families of elliptic curves over finite fields admit ECDLP algorithms asymptotically faster than generic (beyond constant factors), with exact conditions, costs and verified sources; which are class-invariant vs endomorphism-dependent (incl. D3: small-norm elements of Z[pi]); and what is provably NOT a weak family for prime-order curves over prime fields with large embedding degree?
assumptions: Sources verified at search-snippet/abstract level only; items tagged [R] in the report are unverified recollection.
Standard rho step-count heuristic for equivalence classes.
Numerical check restricted to ordinary traces, primes 5<p<3000.

claims: Lemma (proved in report, elementary): for an imaginary quadratic order of discriminant Delta<0, every nonscalar element has norm >= |Delta|/4 ((|Delta|+1)/4 for Delta odd), attained. For Z[pi], N(a+b pi)=a^2+tab+pb^2 >= |t^2-4p|/4, so |t^2-4p| >= c p implies norm >= c p/4; nonscalar units exist iff Delta in {-3,-4}.

Correction to D3 phrasing: End(E) can be a larger order than Z[pi], Delta(End)=D/u^2; extra automorphisms (beyond +-1) need Delta(End) in {-3,-4} (j=0 or 1728), which is a condition on End(E) not on t or |D|; numerically 1392 of 2086 (p,t) pairs with d_K in {-3,-4} have |D|>=p (p<3000).

Rho speedup by Aut equivalence is at most sqrt(#Aut)<=sqrt 6 (<=sqrt 3 beyond negation) for every imaginary quadratic CM field: constant factor; Frobenius acts trivially on E(F_p). Experimental/derivation, standard step-count heuristic only.

Literature classification (metadata-level verification only): faster-than-sqrt(r) families are anomalous (poly time), small embedding degree (pairing + index calculus), Weil descent/GHS for special curves over composite extensions, Gaudry-Diem index calculus for E(F_{q^n}) n>=3 fixed (q^{2-2/n}) and subexponential for some growing-n sequences; Pohlig-Hellman, negation/Aut/Frobenius classes, multi-instance and preprocessing are constant/polylog/amortised factors.

Known-results statement (not a theorem): for prime-order, non-anomalous curves over prime fields with embedding degree > (log p)^c no algorithm faster than O(sqrt r) group operations (up to constant factors) is known to this run; only generic-model lower bounds are proved. Threshold exponent c>=2 is derived here from the heuristic L[1/3] cost, not sourced.
